title: Doubles Detective
subject: math
learningGoal: Use doubles and near doubles (6+6, 6+7) to add quickly.
realWorldHook: Doubles are everywhere: two hands, pairs of shoes, two eyes. They make adding easier.
noPurchaseRoute: Draw dominoes on paper: two boxes with dots.
parentPreview: Your child spots doubles (same on both sides), learns them, then uses a double to work out a near double like 6+7.

parent.parentSays: What things at home come in pairs?
Spread the dominoes out. Ask your child to pick out the doubles and say each one aloud, like 3 and 3 is 6.

child.screen: Find dominoes with the same on both sides!
child.readAloudText: Look for dominoes that match on both sides.

parent.parentSays: If 6 and 6 is 12, what is 6 and 7?
parent.whyThisWorks: Near doubles turn a hard fact into an easy one plus one.

child.readAloudText: Six and six make twelve. So what is six and seven?

parent.parentSays: How did the double help you?

child.readAloudText: How did the double help? Tell your grown-up.

parent.parentSays: Ask the two check questions below. Give your child time to think, then note how each one went.
Which doubles do you know by heart?

misconceptions.signal: Counts every dot rather than using the double.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: You know 5 and 5. Can you use that?
Is 7 more or less than 6? So is the answer more or less than 12?

child.readAloudText: Five and five make ten. What is five and six?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: Two packs of 8 crayons. How many crayons?

child.readAloudText: Two packs of eight crayons. How many crayons?

shorterVersion.description: Go straight to the near-double question.

accessibilityAdaptations: Use objects in two matching rows.
Read the domino dots aloud together.
